stem.en: Growing plants with roots in a nutrient solution, without soil, is called:

explanation.en: Hydroponics (Julius von Sachs, 1860) is used to find essential elements and their deficiency symptoms.
Micronutrients are needed in very small amounts (less than 10 mmol/kg dry matter): Fe, Mn, Cu, Mo, Zn, B, Cl, Ni.

stem.en: Chlorosis of OLDER leaves first suggests a deficiency of a mobile element such as:

explanation.en: Mobile elements (N, K, Mg) are moved from old leaves to young ones, so old leaves show symptoms first.

options.en: is part of the ring of chlorophyll

explanation.en: Mg²⁺ is at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule and activates enzymes of respiration and photosynthesis.

solution.en: Mg²⁺ is at the centre of the chlorophyll molecule and activates enzymes of respiration and photosynthesis.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): An excess of manganese can cause symptoms of iron, magnesium and calcium deficiency.
Reason (R): Manganese competes with Fe and Mg for uptake and with Mg for binding to enzymes, and inhibits calcium translocation to the shoot apex.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Toxicity of one element can appear as deficiency of others. R explains A.

stem.en: The enzyme that reduces N₂ to NH₃ in biological nitrogen fixation is:

explanation.en: Nitrogenase, found only in prokaryotes, reduces N₂ to ammonia and is sensitive to oxygen.
It is an oxygen scavenger, keeping the nodule interior nearly anaerobic; it gives nodules a pink colour.

stem.en: Conversion of ammonia to nitrite and then nitrate is called:

explanation.en: Nitrosomonas/Nitrococcus oxidise NH₃ to NO₂⁻; Nitrobacter oxidises NO₂⁻ to NO₃⁻.
Azotobacter and Beijernickia are free-living aerobic fixers; Rhizobium fixes nitrogen only in symbiosis with legumes.

solution.en: Azotobacter and Beijernickia are free-living aerobic fixers; Rhizobium fixes nitrogen only in symbiosis with legumes.

stem.en: Glutamic acid formed from ammonia and α-ketoglutaric acid can transfer its amino group to other keto acids. This is:

explanation.en: Transamination moves the amino group from one amino acid to a keto acid; it is catalysed by transaminases.
